scope: Local source candidates; no SDK promotion, publication, public API or ownership-contract change
method: Fresh process per measured allocation index; real CRYPTO allocator failure only during client TLS steps. Two additional windows cover every post-ClientHello client handshake step through authentication/completion. Peer and relay allocations are excluded from the injection window. Every run requires terminal retirement or valid completion, fresh-session recovery in the same process, and zero hook-tracked live provider allocations after cleanup.

changes: Each client owns OSSL_LIB_CTX; SSL_CTX_new_ex fetches algorithms from it
Failed lazy algorithm registration cannot retain that client cache in a later session
Constructor rollback releases temporary SSL_CTX references before provider context destruction; drop releases SSL/BIO owners first
Twelfth constructor injection checks private library-context allocation failure and recovery

limitations: Sweeps use the observed healthy-path allocation indices for generated fixture certificates; counts can vary with fixture keys and platform
Provider verification may discard an allocation reason and report terminal Protocol, CertificateRejected or PeerNameMismatch; allocation-cause diagnostics are not guaranteed
Optional failed allocations may be tolerated only with valid handshake/protocol completion
No exhaustive certificate/algorithm/provider matrix, failure-only allocation branches, repeated/simultaneous OOM or Nyra-runtime allocator coverage
macOS/Linux bridge and harness use ASan/UBSan; upstream OpenSSL static libraries are not claimed sanitized; Windows is unsanitized
Independent contexts perform provider initialization per client; no shared-context performance or total memory bound is claimed
macOS x86_64, mobile runtime, complete shutdown/cancellation matrices, SDK promotion and release remain open
